Primero creamos el archivo de 202610_metadata.csv y ponemos en data ese archivo, parametros y los archivos que nos han mandado.


Aqui estoy cambiando el nombre de la columna metadata.csv para que sea igual que mis archivos

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(eDNAfuns)
library(googlesheets4)
library(stringr)


metadata <- read_csv(here("data", "raw_data_tfg", "metadata.csv"))

metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    file1 = str_replace(file1, "_sub.fq", ".fq.gz"),
    file2 = str_replace(file2, "_sub.fq", ".fq.gz")
  ) 

write_csv(metadata, here("data", "raw_data_tfg", "metadata_modificado.csv"))
```

List all ASV tables and Hash keys

```{r}
outputs <- list.dirs(target, recursive = F)
names(outputs) <- c("Dada2", "Vsearch")

outputs %>% 
  map(~list.files(path = .x, pattern="ASV_table.csv", full.names = T) %>% 
        read_csv() %>% 
        summarise(nHashes= n_distinct(Hash),
                  nr     = sum(nReads))) %>% 
  bind_rows(.id="clustering") -> noswarm

outputs %>% 
  map(~list.files(path = .x, pattern="new_ASV*", full.names = T) %>% 
        read_csv() %>% 
        summarise(nHashes= n_distinct(Hash),
                  nr     = sum(nReads))) %>% 
  bind_rows(.id="clustering") -> swarm

bind_rows(swarm %>% mutate(secondary_clustering= "swarm"),
          noswarm %>% mutate(secondary_clustering= "no swarm"))
When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
